title: A chat assistant that troubleshoots the media stack and asks before it changes anything
summary: A local-model assistant that answers media questions by direct message, reads the stack through read-only tools, and runs three writes, each only after a button tap.

stat.label: write actions, each run only after the owner taps Confirm

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Finding out why a show is missing meant opening several apps and reading logs. The household needed one place to ask in plain words: why is this stuck, is the server healthy, do we have this title.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: A direct-message front on an existing Discord bot, backed by a small service that runs a local language model in a tool loop. The model reads the stack through thirteen read-only tools from a triage service that already gave deterministic verdicts. The assistant quotes each verdict and names the tools it read, so an answer can be checked.

The model can propose five actions. Two only read or offer options: a choice among results and an update check. Three are writes, and each needs a tap: a subtitle search, a download and an update apply. The model can only propose them. The bot shows a Confirm button, the button holds a random id, and the action stays in the bot's memory, so a forged button cannot name a different target. A tap works once, within ten minutes, for the owner only.

Credentials arrive through the same deploy path as every other secret, and a script that I run places them. No session handled either value. Merging the code changed nothing until those values were seeded.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: The assistant went live on 7 November 2026. A live test confirmed that a status question returned a real answer, and that a subtitle request produced a Confirm card and then a search that Bazarr accepted. The search had not produced a subtitle by the time I looked 45 seconds later, so I treat the end-to-end result as accepted, not as delivered.

sections.heading: What the first live run found
paragraphs: Review caught two defects before the first deploy. The deploy script read the media credentials but never passed them to the step that writes the configuration, so it would have shipped empty values while printing that they were present. A seed script could also print credentials under shell tracing.

The live test then found a gap in the tool set. Asked what was added recently, the assistant answered with an unrelated status report, because no tool lists recent additions. I added a prompt rule so it says it has no such tool. The real fix is a new read tool in the triage service.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: A status line that says a value is present must test the value the program receives, not the variable in the shell. And when an assistant lacks a tool, it should say so instead of answering a nearby question.
